sentences.tr: thumma radadtu raʾsa jawādī ilā khalfī wa-qad zāda bī al-junūnu fī maḥabbati tilka al-jāriyati wa-rajaʿtu ilā aṣḥābī wa-waṣaftu lahum ḥusnahā wa-jamālahā wa-ḥusna al-shābbi alladhī ʿindahā wa-shajāʿatahu wa-quwwata janānihi wa-kayfa yadhkuru annahu yuṣādimu alfa fārisin
sentences.l: Then I turned the head of my steed to my back, the madness having increased in me in love of that girl; and I returned to my companions and described to them her beauty and her loveliness, and the beauty of the youth who (was) with her, and his courage and the strength of his heart, and how he mentions that he would clash with a thousand horsemen.
sentences.i: Then I turned my horse's head about, the madness of my love for that girl grown worse in me, and rode back to my companions. I described to them her beauty and grace, and the comeliness of the young man who was with her, his courage and stoutness of heart, and how he claimed he would take on a thousand horsemen.
sentences.n: jawādī, “my steed”, and bī, “in me”, end in the undotted yāʾ (ى) the edition often writes for ي. zāda bī al-junūn, “the madness grew upon me”. janān, “heart”, especially as the seat of courage. yuṣādimu, “he clashes with, meets head-on”, verb III of ṣadama.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْلَمْتُ أَصْحَابِي بِجَمِيعِ مَا فِى الْخِبَاءِ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَالتُّحَفِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُمُ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ هَذَا الشَّابَّ مَا هُوَ مُنْقَطِعٌ فِي تِلْكَ الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا لِكَوْنِهِ ذَا شَجَاعَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿlamtu aṣḥābī bi-jamīʿi mā fī al-khibāʾi mina al-amwāli wa-al-tuḥafi wa-qultu lahumu iʿlamū anna hādhā al-shābba mā huwa munqaṭiʿun fī tilka al-arḍi illā li-kawnihi dhā shajāʿatin ʿaẓīmatin
sentences.l: Then I informed my companions of all that (was) in the tent of riches and rarities, and I said to them: Know that this youth, not is he cut-off in that land except for his being possessed-of great courage.
sentences.i: Then I told my companions of all the riches and treasures in the tent, and said to them, “Know that this young man would not be living alone in that country were he not a man of great courage.
sentences.n: aʿlama bi-, “to inform (someone) of”: the bi- marks the thing told. mā huwa … illā li-kawnihi, “he is not … except because of his being”: mā huwa as the negative is common in the edition. munqaṭiʿ, “cut off, isolated”, living apart from any tribe. dhā, “possessed of”, is accusative as the predicate of kawn, “being”.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أُوصِيكُمْ أَنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ قَتَلَ هَذَا الْغُلَامَ يَأْخُذُ أُخْتَهُ فَقَالُوا رَضِينَا بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ūṣīkum anna kulla man qatala hādhā al-ghulāma yaʾkhudhu ukhtahu fa-qālū raḍīnā bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And I enjoin you that every one who kills this lad takes his sister. And they said: We are content with that.
sentences.i: And I lay this down for you: whoever kills this youth shall have his sister.” They said, “We agree to that.”
sentences.n: awṣā, “to charge, enjoin”, here laying down terms. ghulām, “lad, young man”, is used of the youth interchangeably with shābb. raḍiya bi-, “to be content with, accept”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَصْحَابِي لَبِسُوا آلَةَ حَرْبِهِمْ وَرَكِبُوا خَيْلَهُمْ وَقَصَدُوا الْغُلَامَ فَوَجَدُوهُ قَدْ لَبِسَ آلَةَ حَرْبِهِ وَرَكِبَ جَوَادَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna aṣḥābī labisū ālata ḥarbihim wa-rakibū khaylahum wa-qaṣadū al-ghulāma fa-wajadūhu qad labisa ālata ḥarbihi wa-rakiba jawādahu
sentences.l: Then my companions put-on the gear of their war, and mounted their horses and made for the lad; and they found him (that) he had put-on the gear of his war and mounted his steed.
sentences.i: Then my companions put on their armour, mounted their horses and made for the youth; and they found that he too had armed himself and mounted his horse.
sentences.n: ālat al-ḥarb, “the gear of war”, armour and weapons. qaṣada, “to make for, head toward”.

sentences.t: وَوَثَبَتْ إِلَيْهِ أُخْتُهُ وَتَعَلَّقَتْ بِرِكَابِهِ وَبَلَّتْ بُرْقُعَهَا بِدُمُوعِهَا وَهِيَ تُنَادِي بِالْوَيْلِ وَالثُّبُورِ مِنْ خَوْفِهَا عَلَى أَخِيهَا وَتُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-wathabat ilayhi ukhtuhu wa-taʿallaqat bi-rikābihi wa-ballat burquʿahā bi-dumūʿihā wa-hiya tunādī bi-al-wayli wa-al-thubūri min khawfihā ʿalā akhīhā wa-tunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And his sister leapt to him and clung to his stirrup, and wetted her face-veil with her tears, while she was crying-out with woe and ruin from her fear for her brother, and reciting these verses:
sentences.i: His sister sprang to him and clung to his stirrup, soaking her veil with her tears, crying out woe and ruin in her fear for her brother, and she recited these verses:
sentences.n: taʿallaqa bi-, “to cling to”. burquʿ, the face veil. nādā bi-al-wayl wa-al-thubūr, “to cry out woe and perdition”, a set phrase of lament; the bi- introduces what is cried out, and thubūr, “ruin, destruction”, is a Qurʾānic word.

sentences.t:
اِلَى اللّٰهِ اَشْكُوْ مِحْنَةً وَكَابَةً * لَعَلَّ اِلٰهَ الْعَرْشِ يُرْهِقُهُمْ رُعْبَا
يُرِيدُوْنَ قَتْلَكَ يَا اُخَيَّ تَعَمُّدًا * وَلَا شَيْءَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْقِتَالِ وَلَا ذَنْبَا
وَقَدْ عَرَفَتْ ذَا الْخَيْلِ اَنَّكَ فَارِسُ * وَاَشْجَعُ مَنْ حَلَّ الْمَشَارِقَ وَالْغَرْبَا
تُحَامِي عَنِ الْاُخْتِ الَّتِي قَلَّ عَزْمُهَا * فَاَنْتَ اَخُوهَا وَهْيَ تَدْعُو لَكَ الرَّبَّا
فَلَا تَتْرُكِ الْاَعْدَاءَ تَمْلِكُ مُهْجَتِي * وَتَأْخُذُنِي قَهْرًا وَتَأْسِرُنِي غَصْبَا
وَلَسْتُ وَحَقِّ اللّٰهِ اَبْقَى بِبَلْدَةٍ * اِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ فِيهَا وَاِنْ مَلَأَتْ خَصْبَا
وَاَقْتُلُ نَفْسِي فِي هَوَاكَ مَحَبَّةً * وَاَسْكُنُ لَحْدًا فِيهِ اَفْتَرِشُ التُّرْبَا
sentences.tr:
ilā Allāhi ashkū miḥnatan wa-kābatan * laʿalla ilāha al-ʿarshi yurhiquhum ruʿbā
yurīdūna qatlaka yā ukhayya taʿammudan * wa-lā shayʾa min qabli al-qitāli wa-lā dhanbā
wa-qad ʿarafat dhā al-khayli annaka fārisu * wa-ashjaʿu man ḥalla al-mashāriqa wa-al-gharbā
tuḥāmī ʿani al-ukhti allatī qalla ʿazmuhā * fa-anta akhūhā wa-hya tadʿū laka al-rabbā
fa-lā tatruki al-aʿdāʾa tamliku muhjatī * wa-taʾkhudhunī qahran wa-taʾsirunī ghaṣbā
wa-lastu wa-ḥaqqi Allāhi abqā bi-baldatin * idhā lam takun fīhā wa-in malaʾat khaṣbā
wa-aqtulu nafsī fī hawāka maḥabbatan * wa-askunu laḥdan fīhi aftarishu al-turbā
sentences.l:
To God I complain of a trial and a grief; * perhaps the God of the Throne will overwhelm them with terror.
They want your killing, O my little-brother, deliberately, * with no thing before the fighting and no fault.
And these horses have known that you are a knight * and the bravest of whoever has dwelt (in) the easts and the west.
You defend the sister whose resolve has grown-little; * for you are her brother, and she calls on the Lord for you.
So do not leave the enemies to possess my heart's-blood * and take me by force and make-me-captive by violence.
And I will not, by the right of God, remain in a land * if you are not in it, even if it has filled with plenty.
And I will kill my self in your love, out of love, * and dwell in a grave in which I spread-myself the dust.
sentences.i:
To God I make complaint of trial and of grief: * may the Lord of the Throne fill them with dread!
They mean to kill you, little brother, of set purpose, * though nothing came before this fight, and no offence.
These horsemen know you for a knight, * the bravest who has dwelt in east or west.
You shield a sister whose resolve has failed; * you are her brother, and she prays the Lord for you.
Then do not let the foe make my life their own, * and seize me by force, and carry me off captive.
By God's right, I will not stay in any land * where you are not, though it brim with plenty.
I will kill myself for love of you, * and dwell in a grave where I make the dust my bed.
sentences.n: The metre is ṭawīl, every line rhyming in -bā. The print's pointing is kept as given, including kābatan for kaʾāba, “grief”, without its hamza; fārisu without tanwīn; and khaṣbā where the lexica give khiṣb, “plenty”. ukhayya, “my little brother”, is a diminutive of endearment. dhā al-khayli in line 3 reads as “these horses”, that is, these horsemen, with dhā as the demonstrative; the phrase is awkward and may be corrupt. yurhiquhum ruʿbā, “overwhelm them with terror”: ruʿbā, like ghaṣbā and khaṣbā, is an accusative lengthened in rhyme. muhja, “heart's blood, life”. wa-hya, “and she”, is hiya shortened for the metre. iftarasha, “to spread (something) as one's bed”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَخُوهَا شِعْرَهَا بَكَي بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَرَدَّ رَأْسَ جَوَادِهِ إِلَى أُخْتِهِ وَأَجَابَهَا عَلَى شِعْرِهَا بِقَوْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa akhūhā shiʿrahā bakā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-radda raʾsa jawādihi ilā ukhtihi wa-ajābahā ʿalā shiʿrihā bi-qawlihi
sentences.l: And when her brother heard her poetry, he wept a violent weeping, and turned the head of his steed to his sister, and answered her upon her poetry with his saying:
sentences.i: When her brother heard her verses he wept bitterly, turned his horse's head toward his sister, and answered her poem with these lines:
sentences.n: The print writes bakā, “he wept”, with a dotted final yāʾ (بكي), the reverse of its usual ى for ي; the reading is not in doubt. bakā bukāʾan shadīdan, “wept a severe weeping”: the verb is strengthened by its own verbal noun. ajāba ʿalā, “to reply to”.

sentences.t:
قِفِي وَانْظُرِي مِنِّي وُقُوعَ عَجَائِبِ * اِذَا مَا الْتَقَيْنَا حِينَ اُثْخِنُهُمْ ضَرْبَا
وَاِنْ بَرَزَ اللَّيْثُ الْمُقَدَّمُ فِيهِمُ * وَاَشْجَعُهُمْ قَلْبًا وَاَثْبَتُهُمْ لُبًّا
سَاَسْقِيهِ مِنِّي ضَرْبَةً ثَعْلَبِيَّةً * وَاَتْرُكُ فِيهِ الرُّمْحَ يَسْتَغْرِقُ الْكَعْبَا
وَاِنْ لَمْ اُقَاتِلْ عَنْكِ اُخْتِي فَلَيْتَنِي * قَتِيلٌ وَلَيْتَ الطَّيْرَ تَنْهَبُنِي نَهْبَا
اُقَاتِلُ عَنْكِ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ تَكَرُّمًا * وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ بَعْدَنَا يَمْلَأُ الْكُتْبَا
sentences.tr:
qifī wa-unẓurī minnī wuqūʿa ʿajāʾibi * idhā mā iltaqaynā ḥīna uthkhinuhum ḍarbā
wa-in baraza al-laythu al-muqaddamu fīhimu * wa-ashjaʿuhum qalban wa-athbatuhum lubbā
sa-asqīhi minnī ḍarbatan thaʿlabiyyatan * wa-atruku fīhi al-rumḥa yastaghriqu al-kaʿbā
wa-in lam uqātil ʿanki ukhtī fa-laytanī * qatīlun wa-layta al-ṭayra tanhabunī nahbā
uqātilu ʿanki mā istaṭaʿtu takarruman * wa-hādhā ḥadīthun baʿdanā yamlaʾu al-kutbā
sentences.l:
Stop and see from me the falling-out of wonders * when we meet, when I wear-them-down with striking.
And if the lion comes-out, the foremost among them, * and the bravest of them in heart and the firmest of them in mind,
I shall give-him-to-drink from me a Thaʿlabī stroke, * and leave in him the spear sinking-in up to the knot.
And if I do not fight for you, my sister, then would-that-I * were slain, and would-that the birds plunder me a plundering!
I fight for you as far as I am able, out-of-nobility, * and this is a tale that after us will fill the books.
sentences.i:
Stay, and watch the wonders I shall work * when we meet and I hack them down with blows.
And if their foremost lion rides out, * the stoutest-hearted of them and the steadiest of mind,
I shall give him a draught of a Thaʿlabī stroke * and leave my spear in him sunk to the joint.
If I do not fight for you, sister, would I were * slain, and the birds left to tear me as their prey!
I shall fight for you with all my strength, as honour bids, * and this will be a tale to fill the books when we are gone.
sentences.n: The metre is again ṭawīl, and the rhyme in -bā answers hers. The print's pointing is kept as given, including fīhimu with its added ḍamma for the metre, hādhā without the dagger alif, and al-kutbā for al-kutub, “the books”, shortened for the metre. athkhana, “to wear down with wounds”. lubb, “mind, core”. ḍarba thaʿlabiyya, “a Thaʿlabī stroke”, a blow worthy of his clan, the Banū Thaʿlaba. kaʿb, the knot or joint of a spear-shaft: the spear will go in up to it. ʿanki, “for you”, has the feminine -ki, addressed to his sister. takarruman, “out of nobility”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ قَالَ يَا أُخْتِي اسْمَعِي مَا أَقُولُهُ لَكِ وَمَا أُوصِيكِ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi qāla yā ukhtī ismaʿī mā aqūluhu laki wa-mā ūṣīki bihi
sentences.l: And when he had finished from his poetry, he said: O my sister, hear what I say to you and what I charge you with.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses he said, “Sister, listen to what I tell you and to the charge I lay on you.”
sentences.n: faragha min, “to finish (something)”. awṣā bi-, “to charge (someone) with”: the bi- marks the charge.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنْ هَلَكْتُ فَلَا تُمَكِّنِي أَحَدًا مِنْ نَفْسِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan fa-qāla lahā in halaktu fa-lā tumakkinī aḥadan min nafsiki
sentences.l: And she said to him: Hearing and obedience. And he said to her: If I perish, then do not give-power to anyone over your self.
sentences.i: She said to him, “Hearing and obedience.” And he said to her, “If I perish, let no man have you.”
sentences.n: samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan, accusatives standing for an unspoken verb: “(I give) hearing and obedience”. makkana aḥadan min nafsihā, “to give someone power over herself”, that is, to yield herself to him.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ لَطَمَتْ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا وَقَالَتْ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ يَا أَخِي أَنْ أَرَاكَ صَرِيعًا وَأُمَكِّنَ الْأَعْدَاءَ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika laṭamat ʿalā wajhihā wa-qālat maʿādha Allāhi yā akhī an arāka ṣarīʿan wa-umakkina al-aʿdāʾa minnī
sentences.l: And at that she slapped upon her face and said: Refuge of God, O my brother, that I should see you felled and give the enemies power over me!
sentences.i: At that she struck her face and said, “God forbid, brother, that I should see you lying slain and yield myself to the enemy!”
sentences.n: laṭama ʿalā wajhihi, “to slap one's face”, the gesture of mourning. ṣarīʿ, “thrown down, laid low”, of one killed in battle.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ مَدَّ الْغُلَامُ يَدَهُ إِلَيْهَا وَكَشَفَ بُرْقُعَهَا عَنْ وَجْهِهَا فَلَاحَتْ لَنَا صُورَتُهَا كَالشَّمْسِ مِنْ تَحْتِ الْغَمَامِ فَقَبَّلَهَا بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهَا وَوَدَّعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika madda al-ghulāmu yadahu ilayhā wa-kashafa burquʿahā ʿan wajhihā fa-lāḥat lanā ṣūratuhā ka-al-shamsi min taḥti al-ghamāmi fa-qabbalahā bayna ʿaynayhā wa-waddaʿahā
sentences.l: And at that the lad stretched his hand to her and uncovered her veil from her face, and her form shone-out to us like the sun from under the clouds; and he kissed her between her eyes and bade-her-farewell.
sentences.i: Then the youth reached out to her and lifted the veil from her face, and her beauty shone out upon us like the sun from beneath the clouds. He kissed her between the eyes and bade her farewell.
sentences.n: lāḥa, “to appear, gleam”. ṣūra, “form, face”. ghamām, “clouds”. lanā, “to us”: the narrator and his raiders are watching.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيْنَا وَقَالَ لَنَا يَافُرْسَانُ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ ضِيفَانٌ أَوْتُرِيدُونَ الضَّرْبَ وَالطِّعَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika iltafata ilaynā wa-qāla lanā yā fursānu hal antum ḍīfānun aw turīdūna al-ḍarba wa-al-ṭiʿāna
sentences.l: And after that he turned to us and said to us: O horsemen, are you guests, or do you want the striking and the spearing?
sentences.i: Then he turned to us and said, “Horsemen, do you come as guests, or do you want sword-strokes and spear-thrusts?
sentences.n: The print runs yā fursān, “O horsemen”, together as one word (يافرسان), and likewise aw turīdūna, “or do you want” (اوتريدون); the spacing is kept. ḍīfān, plural of ḍayf, “guest”. al-ḍarb wa-al-ṭiʿān, “striking (with the sword) and thrusting (with the spear)”, a stock pair for combat; the youth's challenge falls into rhymed prose in -ān.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ ضِيفَانًا فَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْقِرَى وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُرِيدُونَ الْقَمَرَ الزَّاهِرَ فَلْيَبْرُزْلِي مِنْكُمْ فَارِسٌ بَعْدَ فَارِسٍ فِي هَذَا الْمَيْدَانِ وَمَقَامِ الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-in kuntum ḍīfānan fa-abshirū bi-al-qirā wa-in kuntum turīdūna al-qamara al-zāhira fa-li-yabruz lī minkum fārisun baʿda fārisin fī hādhā al-maydāni wa-maqāmi al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni
sentences.l: For if you are guests, then rejoice in the guest-meal; and if you want the shining moon, then let come-out to me from you horseman after horseman in this field and standing-place of war and spearing.
sentences.i: If you are guests, be glad of the welcome that awaits you; but if it is the shining moon you want, then let your horsemen come out against me one after another, on this field, in the place of war and spear-play.”
sentences.n: abshirū bi-, “rejoice in, take as good news”: the bi- marks the good thing. qirā, the meal owed to a guest by desert custom. al-qamar al-zāhir, “the shining moon”, is his sister. The print runs fa-li-yabruz lī, “then let (him) come out to me”, together as one word (فليبرزلي); the spacing is kept. The rhyme in -ān runs on: al-ṭiʿān, al-maydān, al-ṭiʿān.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بَرَزَ إِلَيْهِ فَارِسٌ شُجَاعٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ الشَّابُّ مَا اسْمُكَ وَمَا اسْمُ أَبِيكَ فَإِنِّي حَالِفٌ أَنِّي مَا أَقْتُلُ مَنِ اسْمُهُ مُوَافِقٌ لِاسْمِي وَاسْمُ أَبِيهِ مُوَافِقٌ لِاسْمِ أَبِي فَإِنْ كُنْتَ بِهَذَا الْوَصْفِ فَقَدْ سَلَّمْتُ إِلَيْكَ الْجَارِيَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika baraza ilayhi fārisun shujāʿun fa-qāla lahu al-shābbu mā ismuka wa-mā ismu abīka fa-innī ḥālifun annī mā aqtulu mani ismuhu muwāfiqun li-ismī wa-ismu abīhi muwāfiqun li-ismi abī fa-in kunta bi-hādhā al-waṣfi fa-qad sallamtu ilayka al-jāriyata
sentences.l: And at that a brave horseman came-out to him, and the youth said to him: What is your name and what is the name of your father? For I am sworn that I do not kill one whose name is matching my name and the name of his father matching the name of my father; so if you are of this description, then I have handed over to you the girl.
sentences.i: Then a brave horseman rode out against him, and the youth said to him, “What is your name, and what is your father's name? For I have sworn never to kill a man whose name is the same as mine and whose father's name is the same as my father's. If you are such a man, the girl is yours: I hand her over to you.”
sentences.n: baraza, “to come out (to single combat)”, the word for a champion stepping forward. ḥālif, “having sworn”, an active participle with the force of a perfect. mā aqtulu, “I do not kill”: mā with the imperfect, the plain negative of the edition. mani ismuhu: man takes a helping kasra before the joined alif. fa-qad sallamtu, “then I have handed over”: the perfect states a promise as though already done.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْفَارِسُ اسْمِي بِلَالٌ فَأَجَابَهُ الشَّابُّ بِقَوْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-fārisu ismī Bilālun fa-ajābahu al-shābbu bi-qawlihi
sentences.l: And the horseman said to him: My name is Bilāl. And the youth answered him with his saying:
sentences.i: The horseman said, “My name is Bilāl,” and the youth answered him in these words:

sentences.t:
كَذَبْتَ فِي قَوْلِكَ مِنْ بِلَالِ * وَجِئْتَ بِالزُّورِ وَبِالْمُحَالِ
اِنْ كُنْتَ شَهْمًا فَاسْتَمِعْ مَقَالِي * اَنَا مُجَنْدِلُ الْاَبْطَالِ فِي الْمَجَالِ
بِصَارِمٍ مَاضٍ كَمَا الْهِلَالِ * فَاصْبِرْ لِطَعْنٍ مُرْجِفِ الْجِبَالِ
sentences.tr:
kadhabta fī qawlika min Bilāli * wa-jiʾta bi-al-zūri wa-bi-al-muḥāli
in kunta shahman fa-istamiʿ maqālī * anā mujandilu al-abṭāli fī al-majāli
bi-ṣārimin māḍin kamā al-hilāli * fa-iṣbir li-ṭaʿnin murjifi al-jibāli
sentences.l:
You have lied in your saying “of Bilāl”, * and you have come with falsehood and with the absurd.
If you are spirited, then listen to my speech: * I am the thrower-down of the heroes in the field,
with a cutting, keen (blade) like the crescent; * so endure a thrust that makes-quake the mountains.
sentences.i:
You lie when you say you are Bilāl, * and bring nothing but falsehood and absurdity.
If you are a man of spirit, hear my words: * I am the one who fells champions on the field
with a keen blade curved like the new moon: * so stand and take a thrust to shake the mountains.
sentences.n: The metre is rajaz, every hemistich rhyming in -ālī. kadhabta … min Bilāli, “you lied in your saying (that you are) of Bilāl”: the min is loose, and the youth seems to take the name for a lie told to come under his oath; the text does not explain further. zūr and muḥāl, “falsehood” and “absurdity”. shahm, “spirited, high-minded”. mujandil, “one who throws (men) to the ground”, from jandala. ṣārim, “cutting”, a sword. kamā al-hilāli, “like the crescent”: kamā directly before a noun is post-classical. murjif al-jibāli, “that makes the mountains quake”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا فَطَعَنَهُ الشَّابُّ فِي صَدْرِهِ فَخَرَجَ السِّنَانُ مِنْ ظَهْرِهِ ثُمَّ بَرَزَ إِلَيْهِ وَاحِدٌ فَقَالَ الشَّابُّ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalā ʿalā baʿḍihimā fa-ṭaʿanahu al-shābbu fī ṣadrihi fa-kharaja al-sinānu min ẓahrihi thumma baraza ilayhi wāḥidun fa-qāla al-shābbu
sentences.l: Then the two charged at each-other, and the young-man thrust him in his chest, and the spear-head went-out from his back. Then there came-out to him one (more), and the young-man said:
sentences.i: Then they charged at each other, and the youth thrust Bilāl through the chest so that the spearhead came out of his back. Then another rode out against him, and the youth said:
sentences.n: ḥamalā ʿalā baʿḍihimā, “they charged upon one another”: baʿḍ with a dual suffix for “each other” is colloquial usage. The man run through is Bilāl, the first challenger. baraza ilā, “to come out against”, is the word for stepping out to single combat; the mubāriz below is the man who does so.

sentences.t:
يَا اَيُّهَا الْكَلْبُ رَخِيمُ الرِّجْسِ * فَاَيْنَ غَالِ سِعْرُهُ مِنْ بَخْسِ
وَاِنَّمَا اللَّيْثُ الْكَرِيمُ الْجِنْسُ * مَنْ لَمْ يُبَالِ فِي الْوَغَى بِنَفْسِ
sentences.tr:
yā ayyuhā al-kalbu rakhīmu al-rijsi * fa-ayna ghāli siʿruhu min bakhsi
wa-innamā al-laythu al-karīmu al-jinsu * man lam yubāli fī al-waghā bi-nafsi
sentences.l:
O you dog, soft of filth, * and where is (one) costly its price from (one) cheap?
And only the lion, the noble of breed, * is he who does not care in the battle-din for a soul.
sentences.i:
You dog, sodden in your foulness, * how far is the costly from the cheap!
The lion of noble breed is only he * who cares nothing for his life in the din of war.
sentences.n: Rajaz, with every hemistich rhyming in -si, the paired-rhyme form usual in battle boasts. The print's pointing is kept as given: the third hemistich ends al-jinsu, with a ḍamma against the -si rhyme (a lapse the prosodists call iqwāʾ); ghāli lacks its tanwīn; and bi-nafsi, “for a soul”, stands where the sense wants bi-nafsihi, “for his own life”. rakhīm al-rijs, literally “soft of filth”, is odd: rakhīm means “soft, gentle”, and the phrase may be corrupt (rajīm, “accursed”, is a candidate); it is rendered as printed. fa-ayna … min …, “where is … from …?”, an idiom for the great distance between two things. al-waghā, “the din of battle”. lam yubāli bi-, “not to care about”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَمْ يُمْهِلْهُ الشَّابُّ دُونَ أَنْ تَرَكَهُ غَرِيقًا فِي دَمِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma lam yumhilhu al-shābbu dūna an tarakahu gharīqan fī damihi
sentences.l: Then the young-man did not give-him-respite short-of that he left him drowned in his blood.
sentences.i: And the youth gave him no respite until he had left him drowned in his own blood.
sentences.n: lam yumhilhu … dūna an tarakahu, “he did not grant him delay short of leaving him”, i.e. he gave him no breathing space before he had left him so. dūna an followed by a perfect verb is Middle Arabic; Classical would have a subjunctive. gharīq, “drowned, sunk”, here in blood.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَادَى الشَّابُّ هَلْ مِنْ مُبَارِزٍ فَبَرَزَ إِلَيْهِ وَاحِدٌ فَانْطَلَقَ عَلَى الشَّابِّ وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma nādā al-shābbu hal min mubārizin fa-baraza ilayhi wāḥidun fa-inṭalaqa ʿalā al-shābbi wa-jaʿala yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then the young-man called-out: Is there any challenger? And there came-out to him one, and he rushed upon the young-man and began saying:
sentences.i: Then the youth called out, “Is there anyone to meet me?” Another came out against him, rushed upon the youth, and began to recite:
sentences.n: hal min mubārizin, “is there any challenger?”, the champion's cry; min after hal means “any at all”. inṭalaqa ʿalā, “to dash at”. jaʿala yaqūlu, “he set about saying”, the usual lead-in to recited verse.

sentences.t:
اِلَيْكَ اَقْبَلْتُ وَفِي قَلْبِي لَهَبْ * مِنْهُ اُنَادِي عِنْدَ صَحْبِي فِي الْحَرْبْ
لَمَّا قَتَلْتَ الْيَوْمَ سَادَاتِ الْعَرَبْ * فَالْيَوْمَ لَا تُلْقِيْ فِكَاكًا مِنْ طَلَبْ
sentences.tr:
ilayka aqbaltu wa-fī qalbī lahab * minhu unādī ʿinda ṣaḥbī fī al-ḥarb
lammā qatalta al-yawma sādāti al-ʿarab * fa-al-yawma lā tulqī fikākan min ṭalab
sentences.l:
To you I have come, and in my heart (is) a flame, * from it I call-out among my comrades in the war;
since you have killed today the lords of the Arabs, * so today you will not throw (find) release from pursuit.
sentences.i:
Against you I come with a flame in my heart, * and for it I cry out among my comrades in war:
since today you have slain the chiefs of the Arabs, * today you will find no escape from the blood-claim.
sentences.n: Rajaz, all four hemistichs rhyming in -ab with the final vowel silenced, as the print points it. The print points tulqī (with a sukūn on its yāʾ), which is the verb “to throw”; the sense wants talqā, “you will meet, find”, and the same pointing recurs in the youth's reply. It is kept as printed. lammā, “since, now that”. fikāk, “release, ransom”; ṭalab, “pursuit”, here the demand for blood-vengeance for the slain chiefs.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشَّابُّ كَلَامَهُ أَجَابَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shābbu kalāmahu ajābahu bi-qawlihi
sentences.l: And when the young-man heard his speech, he answered him with his saying:
sentences.i: When the youth heard his words, he answered him thus:

sentences.t:
كَذَبْتَ بِئْسَ اَنْتَ مِنْ شَيْطَانِ * قَدْ جِئْتَ بِالزُّورِ وَبِالْبُهْتَانِ
اَلْيَوْمَ تُلْقِيْ فَاتِكَ السِّنَانِ * فِي مَوْقِفِ الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ
sentences.tr:
kadhabta biʾsa anta min shayṭāni * qad jiʾta bi-al-zūri wa-bi-al-buhtāni
al-yawma tulqī fātika al-sināni * fī mawqifi al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni
sentences.l:
You lied; wretched are you as a devil! * You have come with the falsehood and with the slander.
Today you will throw (meet) the deadly spear-head * in the standing-place of the war and the thrusting.
sentences.i:
You lie! A wretched devil you are, * come with falsehood and with slander.
Today you shall meet the spearhead that kills * on the field of war and of thrusting.
sentences.n: Rajaz again, rhyming in -āni, answering the challenger in his own metre. biʾsa anta min shayṭānin, “wretched are you as a devil”: biʾsa, “how bad”, with min naming the kind. al-zūr, “falsehood”; al-buhtān, “slander, an outrageous lie”. fātik al-sinān, “the deadly spearhead”: a fātik is one who kills boldly and without warning. mawqif al-ḥarb, “the ground where battle is stood”. tulqī again where talqā, “you will meet”, is meant.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَعَنَهُ فِي صَدْرِهِ فَطَلَعَ السِّنَانُ مِنْ ظَهْرِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭaʿanahu fī ṣadrihi fa-ṭalaʿa al-sinānu min ẓahrihi
sentences.l: Then he thrust him in his chest, and the spear-head came-up out of his back.
sentences.i: Then he thrust him through the chest, and the spearhead came out of his back.
sentences.n: ṭalaʿa, “to come out, emerge”, varies the kharaja of the first kill.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ هَلْ مِنْ مُبَارِزٍ فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ الرَّابِعُ وَسَأَلَهُ الشَّابُّ عَنِ اسْمِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْفَارِسُ اسْمِي هِلَالٌ فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla hal min mubārizin fa-kharaja ilayhi al-rābiʿu wa-saʾalahu al-shābbu ʿani ismihi fa-qāla lahu al-fārisu ismī Hilālun fa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then he said: Is there any challenger? And the fourth went-out to him, and the young-man asked him about his name, and the horseman said to him: My name is Hilāl. And he recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then he cried, “Is there anyone to meet me?” The fourth rider came out to him, and the youth asked him his name. “My name is Hilāl,” said the horseman. And the youth recited:
sentences.n: The youth is keeping his vow to spare only a man whose name and father's name match his own. Hilāl means “crescent moon”, and the youth has just likened his own blade to al-hilāl; the name does not save its bearer. The fourth: Bilāl and the two nameless challengers were the first three. fa-anshada yaqūlu: the reciter is the youth, as the verse shows. The hamza of سأله is the print's.

sentences.t:
اَخْطَأْتَ اِذْ أَرَدْتَ خَوْضَ بَحْرِي * وَجِئْتَ بِالزُّورِ وَكُلِّ الْاَمْرِ
اَنَا الَّذِي تَسْمَعُ مِنِّي شِعْرِي * اَخْتَلِسُ النَّفْسَ وَلَسْتَ تَدْرِي
sentences.tr:
akhṭaʾta idh aradta khawḍa baḥrī * wa-jiʾta bi-al-zūri wa-kulli al-amri
anā alladhī tasmaʿu minnī shiʿrī * akhtalisu al-nafsa wa-lasta tadrī
sentences.l:
You erred when you wanted the wading of my sea, * and you came with the falsehood and every matter.
I am the one from whom you hear my verse; * I snatch the soul and you do not know.
sentences.i:
You erred when you thought to wade into my sea, * and came with falsehood and all its stuff.
I am he whose verse you hear from my lips: * I steal the life away before you know it.
sentences.n: Rajaz, rhyming in -rī. The print's pointing is kept as given, including its own hamza in أَرَدْتَ beside the bare alifs of the rest. khawḍ baḥrī, “wading into my sea”: taking me on. wa-kulli al-amri, “and every matter”, still governed by bi-, is obscure: the line echoes the youth's answer to Bilāl, which has wa-bi-al-muḥāli, “and with the absurd”, and the phrase may be a mere filler or a corruption; it is rendered as printed. akhtalisu al-nafsa, “I snatch away the life”; wa-lasta tadrī, “while you are unaware”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا وَاخْتَلَفَ بَيْنَهُمَا ضَرْبَتَانِ فَكَانَتْ ضَرْبَةُ الشَّابِّ هِيَ السَّابِقَةَ إِلَى الْفَارِسِ فَقَتَلَهُ وَصَارَ كُلُّ مَنْ نَزَلَ إِلَيْهِ يَقْتُلُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalā ʿalā baʿḍihimā wa-ikhtalafa baynahumā ḍarbatāni fa-kānat ḍarbatu al-shābbi hiya al-sābiqata ilā al-fārisi fa-qatalahu wa-ṣāra kullu man nazala ilayhi yaqtuluhu
sentences.l: Then the two charged at each-other, and two blows went-to-and-fro between them, and the blow of the young-man was the one going-first to the horseman, and he killed him; and every one who came-down to him, he took-to killing him.
sentences.i: Then they charged each other and two blows passed between them; but the youth's blow reached the horseman first and killed him. And so it went on: every man who came down against him, he killed.
sentences.n: ikhtalafa baynahumā ḍarbatāni, “two blows went to and fro between them”, a stock phrase of the duel; the verb is singular before its dual subject, as Classical allows. hiya al-sābiqata: hiya separates subject and predicate, and al-sābiqa, “the one that came first”, is the predicate of kānat. wa-ṣāra kullu man nazala ilayhi yaqtuluhu, literally “and every one who came down to him became (such that) he killed him”: ṣāra with an imperfect, “to take to doing”, and a resumptive -hu. nazala, “to come down (into the field)”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرْتُ أَصْحَابِي قَدْ قُتِلُوا قُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي إِنْ نَزَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِى الْحَرْبِ لَمْ أُطِقْهُ وَإِنْ هَرَبْتُ أَبْقَى مَعْيَرَةً بَيْنَ الْعَرَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓartu aṣḥābī qad qutilū qultu fī nafsī in nazaltu ilayhi fī al-ḥarbi lam uṭiqhu wa-in harabtu abqā maʿyaratan bayna al-ʿarabi
sentences.l: And when I saw my companions had been killed, I said in myself: If I go-down to him in the fight, I will not be-equal-to-him; and if I flee, I remain a shame among the Arabs.
sentences.i: When I saw that my companions had been slain, I said to myself, “If I go down to fight him, I shall be no match for him; and if I run, I shall live on as a byword of shame among the Arabs.”
sentences.n: The vowels on نظرتُ and قُتلوا are the print's. naẓara with a direct object, “to see”. lam uṭiqhu, “I would not be equal to him”, from aṭāqa, “to be able for, withstand”. In the conditional, abqā keeps its indicative long vowel where Classical would have the jussive abqa, a Middle Arabic habit. معيرة is read as maʿyara, “a cause of reproach, a disgrace”, from ʿār, shame; muʿayyara, “a reproached (woman)”, is possible on the letters but unlikely of a man speaking of himself.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُمْهِلْنِي الشَّابُّ دُونَ أَنِ انْقَضَّ عَلَيَّ وَجَذَبَنِي بِيَدِهِ فَأَطَاحَنِي مِنْ سَرْجِي فَوَقَعْتُ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yumhilnī al-shābbu dūna ani inqaḍḍa ʿalayya wa-jadhabanī bi-yadihi fa-aṭāḥanī min sarjī fa-waqaʿtu maghshiyyan ʿalayya
sentences.l: And the young-man did not give-me-respite short-of that he swooped upon me and dragged-me with his hand and flung-me from my saddle; and I fell fainted-upon.
sentences.i: But the youth gave me no respite: he swooped down on me, seized me with his hand, and hurled me from my saddle, and I fell senseless.
sentences.n: The shaddas on انقضّ and عليّ are the print's. dūna an with the perfect again, as above. inqaḍḍa ʿalā, “to swoop on”, the word for a falcon's stoop. aṭāḥa, “to send flying, fling down”. maghshiyyan ʿalayya, “fainted”, literally “covered over upon me”: the fixed phrase keeps ʿalā with the pronoun of the one who faints.

sentences.t: وَرَفَعَ سَيْفَهُ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَضْرِبَ عُنُقِي فَتَعَلَّقْتُ بِأَذْيَالِهِ فَحَمَلَنِي بِكَفِّهِ فَصِرْتُ مَعَهُ كَالْعُصْفُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-rafaʿa sayfahu wa-arāda an yaḍriba ʿunuqī fa-taʿallaqtu bi-adhyālihi fa-ḥamalanī bi-kaffihi fa-ṣirtu maʿahu ka-al-ʿuṣfūri
sentences.l: And he raised his sword and wanted to strike my neck; and I clung to his skirts, and he carried-me in his palm, and I became with him like the sparrow.
sentences.i: He raised his sword, meaning to strike off my head, but I clung to the skirts of his garment; and he lifted me in one hand, so that I was like a sparrow in his grasp.
sentences.n: ḍaraba ʿunuqahu, “to strike his neck”, to behead. taʿallaqa bi-adhyālihi, “to cling to someone's skirts”, the gesture of a suppliant begging protection. fa-ṣirtu maʿahu ka-al-ʿuṣfūri, “I became with him like the sparrow”: light and helpless in his hand.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْ ذَلِكَ الْجَارِيَةُ فَرِحَتْ بِفِعْلِ أَخِيهَا وَأَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَتْهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾat dhālika al-jāriyatu fariḥat bi-fiʿli akhīhā wa-aqbalat ʿalayhi wa-qabbalathu bayna ʿaynayhi
sentences.l: And when the girl saw that, she rejoiced at the deed of her brother, and came-forward to him and kissed him between his eyes.
sentences.i: When the girl saw this she rejoiced at her brother's deed; she came up to him and kissed him on the brow.
sentences.n: The hamza of رأت is the print's. Kissing “between the eyes”, on the forehead, returns the kiss he gave her before the fight. fariḥa bi-, “to rejoice at”; aqbala ʿalā, “to come up to, turn to”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ سَلَّمَنِي إِلَى أُخْتِهِ وَقَالَ لَهَا دُونَكِ وَإِيَّاهُ وَأَحْسِنِي مَثْوَاهُ لِأَنَّهُ دَخَلَ فِي زِمَامِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu sallamanī ilā ukhtihi wa-qāla lahā dūnaki wa-iyyāhu wa-aḥsinī mathwāhu li-annahu dakhala fī zimāminā
sentences.l: Then he handed-me-over to his sister and said to her: Before-you, you and him! And make-good his lodging, because he has entered into our halter (protection).
sentences.i: Then he handed me over to his sister and said to her, “He is in your charge. Lodge him well, for he has come under our protection.”
sentences.n: The kasra on دونكِ is the print's, marking the feminine “you”. dūnaki, “before you!”, i.e. “take it, it is yours”, an adverb used as a command; with wa-iyyāhu, “you and him”, it hands the captive over. aḥsinī mathwāhu, “make his dwelling good”, i.e. treat him as an honoured guest, a phrase from the Qurʾān (Joseph 12:21). zimām, “halter-rope”, hence “charge, protection”: one who enters another's zimām becomes his protected dependant.

sentences.t: فَقَبَضَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ عَلَى أَطْوَاقِ دِرْعِي وَصَارَتْ تَقُودُنِي كَمَا تَقُودُ الْكَلْبَ
sentences.tr: fa-qabaḍati al-jāriyatu ʿalā aṭwāqi dirʿī wa-ṣārat taqūdunī ka-mā taqūdu al-kalba
sentences.l: And the girl took-hold of the collars of my mail-coat and began leading-me as she leads the dog.
sentences.i: The girl took hold of the collar of my mail-coat and led me along as one leads a dog.
sentences.n: qabaḍa ʿalā, “to grip, seize”. aṭwāq, plural of ṭawq, “collar, neck-ring”, here the neck of the coat of mail. ṣārat taqūdunī, “she took to leading me”.

sentences.t: وَفَكَّتْ عَنْ أَخِيهَا لَأْمَةَ الْحَرْبِ وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ بَدْلَةً وَنَصَبَتْ لَهُ كُرْسِيًّا مِنَ الْعَاجِ فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-fakkat ʿan akhīhā laʾmata al-ḥarbi wa-albasathu badlatan wa-naṣabat lahu kursiyyan mina al-ʿāji fa-jalasa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And she unfastened from her brother the armour of war, and clothed-him (in) a suit, and set-up for him a chair of the ivory, and he sat on it.
sentences.i: She unbuckled her brother's war-harness and dressed him in a fresh suit of clothes, and set up an ivory chair for him, and he sat down on it.
sentences.n: laʾmat al-ḥarb, “the gear of war”, a full suit of armour; the print writes the word without its hamza, لامة. badla, “a suit of clothes, a change of dress”, a post-classical word.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ بَيَّضَ اللَّهُ عِرْضَكَ وَجَعَلَكَ عُدَّةً لِلنَّائِبَاتِ فَأَجَابَهَا بِهَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu bayyaḍa Allāhu ʿirḍaka wa-jaʿalaka ʿuddatan li-al-nāʾibāti fa-ajābahā bi-hādhihi al-abyāti
sentences.l: And she said to him: May God whiten your honour and make-you a provision for the calamities! And he answered her with these verses:
sentences.i: And she said to him, “May God keep your honour unstained, and make you a shield held ready against misfortune!” And he answered her in these lines:
sentences.n: The shadda on بيّض is the print's. bayyaḍa Allāhu ʿirḍaka, “may God whiten your honour”, i.e. keep your good name spotless, a common blessing. ʿudda, “equipment, something kept in readiness”; al-nāʾibāt, “the blows of fortune”.

sentences.t:
تَقُولُ وَقَدْ رَأَتْ فِى الْحَرْبِ أُخْتِي * لَوَامِعَ غُرَّتِي مِثْلَ الشُّعَاعِ
اَلَا لِلّٰهِ دَرُّكَ مِنْ شُجَاعِ * تَذَلُّ لِحَرْبِهِ اُسْدُ الْبِقَاعِ
فَقُلْتُ لَهَا سَلِي الْاَبْطَالَ عَنِّي * اِذَا مَا فَرَّ اَرْبَابُ الْقِرَاعِ
اَنَا الْمَعْرُوفُ فِي سَعْدِي وَجَدِّي * وَعَزْمِي قَدْ عَلَا اَيَّ ارْتِفَاعِ
اَيَا حَمَّادُ قَدْ نَازَلْتَ لَيْثًا * يُرِيكَ الْمَوْتَ يَسْعَى كَالْاَفَاعِي
sentences.tr:
taqūlu wa-qad raʾat fī al-ḥarbi ukhtī * lawāmiʿa ghurratī mithla al-shuʿāʿi
alā li-llāhi durruka min shujāʿi * tadhillu li-ḥarbihi usdu al-biqāʿi
fa-qultu lahā salī al-abṭāla ʿannī * idhā mā farra arbābu al-qirāʿi
anā al-maʿrūfu fī saʿdī wa-jaddī * wa-ʿazmī qad ʿalā ayya irtifāʿi
ayā Ḥammādu qad nāzalta laythan * yurīka al-mawta yasʿā ka-al-afāʿī
sentences.l:
She says, and she has seen in the war, my sister, * the gleamings of my blaze like the sunbeam:
“Ah, to God (is) your milk, of a hero, * to whose warring the lions of the valleys are humbled!”
And I said to her: Ask the champions about me * when the lords of the clash flee.
I am the known-one in my fortune and my luck, * and my resolve has risen what a rising!
O Ḥammād, you have met-in-combat a lion * who shows you death running like the vipers.
sentences.i:
My sister, seeing in the battle * my brow flash bright as a sunbeam, says:
“How splendid you are, a hero, God bless you, * whose onslaught brings the lions of the valleys low!”
And I tell her, “Ask the champions about me, * when the masters of the sword-clash turn and run.
I am the man renowned for fortune and luck, * and my resolve has climbed as high as high can go.”
Ḥammād, you have come down to fight a lion * who shows you death gliding toward you like a viper.
sentences.n: Wāfir, rhyming in -āʿī. The print's pointing is kept as given, including فِى with an undotted final yāʾ and the print's own hamza in رَأَتْ and أُخْتِي. ghurra is the white blaze on a horse's forehead, used of a warrior's shining brow. li-llāhi durruka, “to God belongs your milk”, i.e. the milk you were nursed on, a fixed cry of admiration; min shujāʿi, “as a hero!”, specifies it. al-biqāʿ, “low-lying lands, valleys”. al-qirāʿ, “the clash of weapons”. saʿd and jadd both mean good fortune. ayya irtifāʿi, “what a rising!”, an admiring exclamation. The sister's words fill the second line; in the last line the youth turns to his captive and names him. yasʿā, “runs, goes about”, of snakes “glides”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ شِعْرَهُ حِرْتُ فِي أَمْرِي وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى حَالَتِي وَمَا صِرْتُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْأَسْرِ وَتَصَاغَرَتْ إِلَيَّ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu shiʿrahu ḥirtu fī amrī wa-naẓartu ilā ḥālatī wa-mā ṣirtu ilayhi mina al-asri wa-taṣāgharat ilayya nafsī
sentences.l: And when I heard his poetry, I became-perplexed in my affair, and I looked at my state and what I had come to of captivity, and my soul grew-small to me.
sentences.i: When I heard his verses I was at a loss what to do. I looked at my plight and at the captivity I had come to, and I shrank in my own eyes.
sentences.n: ḥirtu, “I was bewildered” (ḥāra, yaḥīru). taṣāghara, “to grow small, be humbled”; taṣāgharat ilayya nafsī, literally “my soul grew small to me”: I felt myself diminished. The shadda on اليّ is the print's.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرْتُ إِلَى الْجَارِيَةِ أُخْتِ الشَّابِّ وَإِلَى حُسْنِهَا فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي هَذِهِ سَبَبُ الْفِتْنَةِ وَصِرْتُ أَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْ جَمَالِهَا وَأَجْرَيْتُ الْعَبَرَاتِ وَأَنْشَدْتُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓartu ilā al-jāriyati ukhti al-shābbi wa-ilā ḥusnihā fa-qultu fī nafsī hādhihi sababu al-fitnati wa-ṣirtu ataʿajjabu min jamālihā wa-ajraytu al-ʿabarāti wa-anshadtu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then I looked at the girl, the sister of the youth, and at her beauty, and I said in myself: This-one is the cause of the trouble; and I began wondering at her loveliness, and I made-flow the tears, and I recited these verses:
sentences.i: Then I looked at the girl, the young man's sister, and at her beauty, and said to myself, “She is the cause of all this trouble.” I fell to marvelling at her loveliness; my tears ran, and I recited these verses:
sentences.n: hādhihi sababu al-fitnati, “this one is the cause of the trouble”: the feminine demonstrative agrees with the girl it points to, not with the masculine sabab. fitna is both “temptation” and “strife”, and both are meant: her beauty brought on the fight. ṣirtu ataʿajjabu, “I began to marvel”: ṣāra with an imperfect, “to begin to, fall to”, is a favourite of the later language.

sentences.t:
خَلِيلِي كُفَّ عَنْ لَوْمِي وَعَذْلِي * فَاِنِّي لِلْمَلَامَةِ غَيْرُ وَاعِ
كُلِفْتُ بِغَادَةٍ لَمْ تُبْدِ اِلَّا * دَعَتْنِي فِي مَحَبَّتِهَا الدَّوَاعِي
اَخُوهَا فِى الْهَوَى اَمْسَى رَقِيبِي * وَصَاحِبُ هِمَّةٍ وَطَوِيلُ بَاعِ
sentences.tr:
khalīlī kuffa ʿan lawmī wa-ʿadhlī * fa-innī li-al-malāmati ghayru wāʿī
kuliftu bi-ghādatin lam tubdi illā * daʿatnī fī maḥabbatihā al-dawāʿī
akhūhā fī al-hawā amsā raqībī * wa-ṣāḥibu himmatin wa-ṭawīlu bāʿī
sentences.l:
My friend, hold-back from my blame and my reproach, * for I to reproach am not heeding.
I am-smitten with a tender-maiden; she did not show-herself but * the summoners summoned me to her love.
Her brother in love has-become my watcher, * a man of resolve and long of arm-span.
sentences.i:
Friend, spare me your blame and reproach; * I do not listen to reproof.
I am smitten with a supple maid: she had only to appear * and every call of the heart summoned me to love her.
Her brother stands guard over my love, * a man of high resolve and long reach.
sentences.n: Wāfir metre, rhyming in -āʿī: the same metre and rhyme as ʿAbbād's poem just before, which Ḥammād here answers. The print's pointing is kept as given, including فِى with undotted final yāʾ in the last line. kuliftu bi-, “I am smitten with”: the print points it as a passive, where the dictionaries give kalifa bi-, “to be passionately fond of”. ghāda, a soft, supple young woman. lam tubdi illā daʿatnī …, “she did not show herself but … called me”: she had only to appear. raqīb, the watcher of love poetry, who keeps the lover from the beloved. ṭawīl al-bāʿ, “long of arm-span”, powerful, able. wāʿī and bāʿī: wāʿin, “heeding”, and bāʿ, “arm-span”, with the final vowel drawn out for the rhyme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ أَحْضَرَتْ لِأَخِيهَا الطَّعَامَ فَدَعَانِي إِلَى الْأَكْلِ مَعَهُ فَفَرِحْتُ وَأَمِنْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي مِنَ الْقَتْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-jāriyata aḥḍarat li-akhīhā al-ṭaʿāma fa-daʿānī ilā al-akli maʿahu fa-fariḥtu wa-amintu ʿalā nafsī mina al-qatli
sentences.l: Then the girl brought for her brother the food, and he invited me to the eating with him; and I rejoiced and felt-safe for my life from the killing.
sentences.i: Then the girl brought her brother his meal, and he invited me to eat with him; and I was glad, and felt my life safe from being killed.
sentences.n: amintu ʿalā nafsī, “I felt secure for myself”. To be asked to share a man's food was to be under his protection; hence Ḥammād's relief.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا فَرَغَ أَخُوهَا مِنَ الْأَكْلِ أَحْضَرَتْ لَهُ آنِيَةَ الْمُدَامِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشَّابَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْمُدَامِ وَشَرِبَ حَتَّى شَعْشَعَ الشَّرَابُ فِي رَأْسِهِ وَاحْمَرَّ وَجْهُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā faragha akhūhā mina al-akli aḥḍarat lahu āniyata al-mudāmi thumma inna al-shābba aqbala ʿalā al-mudāmi wa-shariba ḥattā shaʿshaʿa al-sharābu fī raʾsihi wa-iḥmarra wajhuhu
sentences.l: And when her brother had finished from the eating, she brought him the vessels of the wine; then the youth turned-to the wine and drank until the drink sparkled in his head and his face reddened.
sentences.i: When her brother had done eating, she brought him the wine-vessels. The young man set to the wine and drank until it sparkled in his head and his face flushed red.
sentences.n: āniya, “vessels” (plural of ināʾ). mudām, “wine”, a poetic word, properly “what is kept long (in the jar)”. aqbala ʿalā, “to turn to, set about”. shaʿshaʿa, “to shine, sparkle”; said of wine, to go to the head. The shadda on احمرّ is the print's.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ إِلَيَّ وَقَالَ لِي وَيْلَكَ يَا حَمَّادُ هَلْ تَعْرِفُنِي أَمْ لَا فَقُلْتُ وَعَيْشِكَ مَا ازْدَدْتُ إِلَّا جَهْلًا
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ilayya wa-qāla lī waylaka yā Ḥammādu hal taʿrifunī am lā fa-qultu wa-ʿayshika mā izdadtu illā jahlan
sentences.l: And he turned to me and said to me: Woe-to-you, O Ḥammād, do you know me or not? And I said: By your life, I have not increased except in ignorance.
sentences.i: He turned to me and said, “Confound you, Ḥammād, do you know who I am or not?” I said, “By your life, the more I look, the less I know.”
sentences.n: waylaka, “woe to you”, here rough familiarity rather than a curse; the fatḥa on its lām is the print's, as are the shaddas on اليّ and الّا. wa-ʿayshika, “by your life”, an oath. mā izdadtu illā jahlan, “I have only grown more ignorant”: I have no idea who you are.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا حَمَّادُأَ نَا عَبَّادُ بْنُ تَمِيمِ بْنِ ثَعْلَبَةَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَهَبَ لَكَ نَفْسَكَ وَأَبْقَى عَلَيْكَ عِرْسَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Ḥammādu anā ʿAbbādu ibnu Tamīmi ibni Thaʿlabata inna Allāha wahaba laka nafsaka wa-abqā ʿalayka ʿirsaka
sentences.l: And he said: O Ḥammād, I am ʿAbbād son of Tamīm son of Thaʿlaba. God has granted you your soul, and spared for you your wife.
sentences.i: He said, “Ḥammād, I am ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm ibn Thaʿlaba. God has given you your life, and spared you to your wife.”
sentences.n: The print sets yā Ḥammādu anā, “O Ḥammād, I (am)”, as يا حمادا نا, the alif of anā joined to the name; the spacing is kept and the words are pointed as they are said. ibn, “son”, is written without its alif between two names (بن), as usual. wahaba laka nafsaka, “granted you your life”: ʿAbbād had spared him in the fight. ʿirs is “wife” (also “bride”), and abqā ʿalā “to spare, preserve for”: Ḥammād's wife is not made a widow. The word could also be read ʿurs, “wedding”, which fits less well.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَيَّانِي بِقَدَحٍ شَرِبْتُهُ وَحَيَّانِي بِثَانٍ وَثَالِثٍ وَرَابِعٍ فَشَرِبْتُ الْجَمِيعَ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥayyānī bi-qadaḥin sharibtuhu wa-ḥayyānī bi-thānin wa-thālithin wa-rābiʿin fa-sharibtu al-jamīʿa
sentences.l: Then he toasted-me with a cup; I drank it; and he toasted-me with a second and a third and a fourth, and I drank them all.
sentences.i: Then he pledged me in a cup, which I drank, and pledged me in a second, a third and a fourth; and I drank them all.
sentences.n: ḥayyā bi-, “to greet with”, here to hand a cup in salutation, to pledge. The shadda on the first حيّاني is the print's. thānin, “a second”, with the shortened ending of nouns in -ī.

sentences.t: وَنَادَمَنِي وَحَلَّفَنِي أَنِّي لَا أَخُونُهُ فَحَلَفْتُ لَهُ أَلْفًا وَخَمْسَمِائَةِ يَمِينٍ أَنِّي لَا أَخُونُهُ قَطُّ بَلْ أَكُونُ لَهُ مُعِينًا
sentences.tr: wa-nādamanī wa-ḥallafanī annī lā akhūnuhu fa-ḥalaftu lahu alfan wa-khamsamiʾati yamīnin annī lā akhūnuhu qaṭṭu bal akūnu lahu muʿīnan
sentences.l: And he drank-with-me as boon-companion, and made-me-swear that I would not betray him; and I swore to him a thousand and five-hundred oaths that I would not betray him ever, but would be to him a helper.
sentences.i: He kept me company over the wine, and made me swear that I would not betray him; and I swore him fifteen hundred oaths that I would never betray him, but would stand by him as a helper.
sentences.n: nādama, “to be someone's drinking companion” (nadīm). ḥallafa, “to make (someone) swear”, causative of ḥalafa. khamsamiʾa, “five hundred”, is written as one word; yamīn, “oath”, is also “right hand”. qaṭṭu, “ever”, belongs properly with a past verb; here it goes with the imperfect, as in later Arabic.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَ أُخْتَهُ أَنْ تَأْتِيَنِي بِعَشْرِ خِلَعٍ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ فَأَتَتْ بِهَا وَأَفْرَغَتْهَا عَلَى بَدَنِي وَهَذِهِ بَدْلَةٌ مِنْهَا عَلَى جَسَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara ukhtahu an taʾtiyanī bi-ʿashri khilaʿin mina al-ḥarīri fa-atat bihā wa-afraghathā ʿalā badanī wa-hādhihi badlatun minhā ʿalā jasadī
sentences.l: And at that he commanded his sister that she bring me ten robes of silk; and she brought them, and poured-them over my body; and this is a suit of them on my body.
sentences.i: Thereupon he told his sister to bring me ten robes of honour in silk. She brought them and clothed me in them; and this suit I am wearing is one of them.
sentences.n: khilaʿ, plural of khilʿa, a robe of honour. afraghahā ʿalā badanī, “poured them over my body”, dressed me in them. Ḥammād points to what he has on: the dead man's gifts are his proof.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَهَا أَنْ تَأْتِيَنِي بِنَاقَةٍ مِنْ أَحْسَنِ النِّيَاقِ فَأَتَتْنِي بِنَاقَةٍ مُحَمَّلَةٍ مِنَ التُّحَفِ وَالزَّادِ
sentences.tr: wa-amarahā an taʾtiyanī bi-nāqatin min aḥsani al-niyāqi fa-atatnī bi-nāqatin muḥammalatin mina al-tuḥafi wa-al-zādi
sentences.l: And he commanded her that she bring me a she-camel of the finest of the she-camels; and she brought me a she-camel laden with the rarities and the provisions.
sentences.i: He told her to bring me a she-camel, one of the finest there were, and she brought me a she-camel laden with precious things and provisions.
sentences.n: muḥammala min, “loaded with”: min where Classical would say bi-. tuḥaf, plural of tuḥfa, a rare and precious thing, a present.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَهَا أَيْضًا أَنْ تُحْضِرَ لِي الْحِصَانَ الْأَشْقَرَ فَأَحْضَرَتْهُ لِي ثُمَّ وَهَبَ لِي جَمِيعَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-amarahā ayḍan an tuḥḍira lī al-ḥiṣāna al-ashqara fa-aḥḍarathu lī thumma wahaba lī jamīʿa dhālika
sentences.l: And he commanded her also that she bring for me the sorrel stallion, and she brought it for me; then he gave to me all of that.
sentences.i: He told her also to bring me the sorrel stallion, and she brought it; and then he made me a gift of it all.
sentences.n: ashqar, “sorrel, chestnut”, of a reddish horse.

sentences.t: وَأَقَمْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فِي أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ وَالَّذِي قَدْ أَعْطَاهُ لِي مَوْجُودٌ عِنْدِي إِلَى الْآنَ
sentences.tr: wa-aqamtu ʿindahum thalāthata ayyāmin fī aklin wa-shurbin wa-alladhī qad aʿṭāhu lī mawjūdun ʿindī ilā al-āna
sentences.l: And I stayed with them three days in eating and drinking; and what he gave to me is present with me until now.
sentences.i: I stayed with them three days, eating and drinking, and what he gave me I have with me to this day.
sentences.n: thalātha, “three”, is written defectively, with the dagger alif. aʿṭāhu lī, “gave it to me”, with the li- of the spoken language.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ الثَّلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ قَالَ لِي يَا أَخِي يَا حَمَّادُ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَنَامَ قَلِيلًا لِأُرِيحَ نَفْسِي وَقَدِ اسْتَأْمَنْتُكَ عَلَى نَفْسِي فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ خَيْلًا ثَائِرَةً فَلَا تَفْزَعْ مِنْهَا وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَنِي ثَعْلَبَةَ يَطْلُبُونَ حَرْبِي
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda al-thalāthati ayyāmin qāla lī yā akhī yā Ḥammādu urīdu an anāma qalīlan li-urīḥa nafsī wa-qadi istaʾmantuka ʿalā nafsī fa-in raʾayta khaylan thāʾiratan fa-lā tafzaʿ minhā wa-iʿlam annahum min banī Thaʿlabata yaṭlubūna ḥarbī
sentences.l: And after the three days he said to me: O my brother, O Ḥammād, I want to sleep a little to rest myself, and I have entrusted-you with my life; so if you see horses rising-up, do not be-alarmed at them, and know that they are of the sons of Thaʿlaba, seeking war with me.
sentences.i: After the three days he said to me, “Ḥammād, my brother, I want to sleep a little and rest. I have put my life in your keeping. If you see horsemen coming on, do not be alarmed by them: know that they are of the Banū Thaʿlaba, come to make war on me.”
sentences.n: al-thalāthati ayyāmin, “the three days”, with the article on the numeral rather than on the counted noun, a common later usage. istaʾmana ʿalā, “to entrust (someone) with”; the hamza is the print's, as in raʾayta. khayl thāʾira, “horses rising up”, horsemen coming on in a cloud of dust: khayl, “horses”, stands for the riders and takes a feminine adjective, then a masculine plural pronoun, annahum. ʿAbbād's own grandfather is Thaʿlaba; the text does not say whether these are his kin at feud with him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَسَّدَ سَيْفَهُ تَحْتَ رَأْسِهِ وَنَامَ
sentences.tr: thumma tawassada sayfahu taḥta raʾsihi wa-nāma
sentences.l: Then he pillowed-on his sword under his head, and slept.
sentences.i: Then he laid his head on his sword for a pillow, and slept.
sentences.n: The print has توسل, a misprint for توسد, corrected here. tawassada, “to take as a pillow (wisāda)”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَغْرَقَ فِى النَّوْمِ وَسْوَسَ إِلَيَّ إِبْلِيسُ بِقَتْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaghraqa fī al-nawmi waswasa ilayya Iblīsu bi-qatlihi
sentences.l: And when he was-sunk in the sleep, Iblīs whispered to me of killing-him.
sentences.i: And when he was sunk deep in sleep, the Devil whispered to me to kill him.
sentences.n: istaghraqa fī al-nawm, “to be drowned in sleep”, sound asleep. waswasa ilā … bi-, “to whisper (temptation) to someone to do”: the word for the Devil's insinuation, as in the Qurʾān. Iblīs is the Devil's proper name. The shadda on اليّ is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَجَذَبْتُ سَيْفَهُ مِنْ تَحْتِ رَأْسِهِ وَضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبَةً أَطَاحَتْ رَأْسَهُ عَنْ جُثَّتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu bi-surʿatin wa-jadhabtu sayfahu min taḥti raʾsihi wa-ḍarabtuhu ḍarbatan aṭāḥat raʾsahu ʿan juththatihi
sentences.l: So I rose with speed, and pulled his sword from under his head, and struck him a stroke that sent-flying his head from his body.
sentences.i: I got up quickly, drew his sword from under his head, and struck him a blow that sent his head flying from his body.
sentences.n: aṭāḥa, “to make fall, send flying”. juththa, “body, trunk”, often of a corpse.

sentences.t: فَعَلِمَتْ بِي أُخْتُهُ فَوَثَبَتْ مِنْ جَانِبِ الْخِبَاءِ وَرَمَتْ نَفْسَهَا عَلَى أَخِيهَا وَشَقَّتْ مَا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الثِّيَابِ وَأَنْشَدَتْ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalimat bī ukhtuhu fa-wathabat min jānibi al-khibāʾi wa-ramat nafsahā ʿalā akhīhā wa-shaqqat mā ʿalayhā mina al-thiyābi wa-anshadat hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And his sister came-to-know of me, and leapt from the side of the tent, and threw herself upon her brother, and rent what was on her of the clothes, and recited these verses:
sentences.i: His sister became aware of what I had done. She sprang up from the side of the tent, threw herself on her brother, tore the clothes she wore, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: ʿalima bi-, “to learn of, become aware of”. Rending one's garments is the gesture of mourning. The shadda on شقّت is the print's.

sentences.t:
اِلَى الْاَهْلِ بَلِّغْ اِنَّ ذَا اَشْأَمُ الْخَبَرْ * وَمَا لِامْرِئٍ مِمَّا الْحَكِيمُ قَضَى مَفَرْ
وَاَنْتَ صَرِيعٌ يَا اَخِيْ مُتَجَنْدِلٌ * وَوَجْهُكَ يَحْكِي حُسْنُهُ دَوْرَةَ الْقَمَرْ
لَقَدْ كَانَ يَوْمُ الشُّوْمِ يَوْمَ لَقِيتَهُمْ * وَرُمْحُكَ مِنْ بَعْدِ اِطِّرَادٍ قَدِ انْكَسَرْ
وَبَعْدَكَ لَا يَرْتَاحُ لِلْخَيْلِ رَاكِبٌ * وَلَا تَلِدُ الْاُنْثَى نَظِيرُكَ مِنْ ذَكَرْ
وَاَصْبَحَ حَمَّادُ لَكَ الْيَوْمَ قَاتِلًا * وَقَدْ خَانَ اَيْمَانًا وَبِالْعَهْدِ قَدْ غَدَرْ
يُرِيْدُ بِهٰذَا اَنْ يَنَالَ مُرَادَهُ * لَقَدْ كَذَبَ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي كُلِّ مَا اَمَرْ
sentences.tr:
ilā al-ahli balligh inna dhā ashʾamu al-khabar * wa-mā li-imriʾin mimmā al-ḥakīmu qaḍā mafar
wa-anta ṣarīʿun yā akhī mutajandilun * wa-wajhuka yaḥkī ḥusnuhu dawrata al-qamar
laqad kāna yawmu al-shūmi yawma laqītahum * wa-rumḥuka min baʿdi iṭṭirādin qadi inkasar
wa-baʿdaka lā yartāḥu li-al-khayli rākibun * wa-lā talidu al-unthā naẓīruka min dhakar
wa-aṣbaḥa Ḥammādu laka al-yawma qātilan * wa-qad khāna aymānan wa-bi-al-ʿahdi qad ghadar
yurīdu bi-hādhā an yanāla murādahu * laqad kadhaba al-shayṭānu fī kulli mā amar
sentences.l:
To the kinsfolk convey: this is the most ill-omened of the tidings, * and there is not for a man, from what the All-Wise decreed, an escape.
And you (lie) felled, O my brother, flung-to-the-ground, * and your face, its beauty resembles the round of the moon.
Truly the day of ill-omen was the day you met them, * and your spear, after charging, has broken.
And after you no rider takes-delight in the horses, * nor bears the female your like of a male.
And Ḥammād has become for you today a killer; * he has betrayed oaths, and the covenant he has broken.
He wants by this to attain his desire; * truly the Satan has lied in all that he commanded.
sentences.i:
Carry to our people this, the most ill-starred of tidings: * from what the All-Wise decrees no man escapes.
You lie felled, my brother, stretched on the stones, * your face in its beauty the full round of the moon.
The day you met them was a day of evil omen; * after the charge your spear lies broken.
After you no rider will delight in horses, * nor will woman bear a son your equal.
Today Ḥammād has become your murderer: * he has betrayed his oaths and broken faith.
By this he means to win his desire; * but Satan lies in all he commands.
sentences.n: Ṭawīl metre, rhyming in -ar with the final consonant unvowelled (a “restricted” rhyme): khabar, mafar, qamar, inkasar, dhakar, ghadar, amar. The print's pointing is kept as given: اَخِيْ and يُرِيْدُ with a sukūn on the long vowel; الشُّوْمِ for shuʾm, “ill omen”, with the hamza softened to w; نَظِيرُكَ in the nominative where talidu wants an object (naẓīraka); and حَمَّادُ without nunation, for the metre. al-ḥakīm, “the All-Wise”, is God. mutajandil, “thrown down on the hard ground” (jandal, stones). iṭṭirād, “running on, charging”. The lament speaks as if ʿAbbād fell in battle, though he was killed asleep: such poems are often fitted to a story rather than made for it. The last line turns Ḥammād's own excuse against him: the Devil lies in all he bids.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا قَالَتْ لَهُ يَا مَلْعُونَ الْجَدَّيْنِ لِمَا ذَا قَتَلْتَ أَخِي وَخُنْتَهُ وَكَانَ مُرَادُهُ أَنْ يَرُدَّكَ إِلَى بِلَادِكَ بِالزَّادِ وَالْهَدَايَا وَكَانَ مُرَادُهُ أَيْضًا أَنْ يُزَوِّجَنِي لَكَ فِى أَوَّلِ الشَّهْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā qālat lahu yā malʿūna al-jaddayni li-mā dhā qatalta akhī wa-khuntahu wa-kāna murāduhu an yaruddaka ilā bilādika bi-al-zādi wa-al-hadāyā wa-kāna murāduhu ayḍan an yuzawwijanī laka fī awwali al-shahri
sentences.l: And when she had finished from her poetry, she said to him: O cursed of the two grandfathers, for what did you kill my brother and betray him, when his intent was to send-you-back to your country with the provisions and the gifts, and his intent was also to marry me to you at the beginning of the month?
sentences.i: When she had finished her verses she said to him, “Accursed on both sides of your line! Why did you kill my brother and betray him? He meant to send you home to your own country with provisions and gifts, and he meant, too, to give me to you in marriage at the start of the month.”
sentences.n: qālat lahu, “she said to him”: Ḥammād is telling his own story, and the text slips here for a moment from “me” to “him”. yā malʿūna al-jaddayni, “O you whose two grandfathers are cursed”, accursed by descent on the father's side and the mother's. The print splits li-mā dhā, “why”, in two (لما ذا); the spacing is kept. The ḍamma on خُنته is the print's. wa-kāna murāduhu, “and his intent was”, carries the force of “when he meant”. yuzawwijanī laka, “marry me to you”, with li- as in the spoken language, where Classical says yuzawwijuka iyyāya.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَذَبَتْ سَيْفًا كَانَ عِنْدَهَا وَجَعَلَتْ قَائِمَهُ فِى الْأَرْضِ وَطَرَفَهُ فِي صَدْرِهَا وَانْحَنَتْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى طَلَعَ مِنْ ظَهْرِهَا فَخَرَّتْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مَيِّتَةً
sentences.tr: thumma jadhabat sayfan kāna ʿindahā wa-jaʿalat qāʾimahu fī al-arḍi wa-ṭarafahu fī ṣadrihā wa-inḥanat ʿalayhi ḥattā ṭalaʿa min ẓahrihā fa-kharrat ʿalā al-arḍi mayyitatan
sentences.l: Then she drew a sword that was with her, and set its hilt in the ground and its point in her breast, and bent over upon it until it came-out from her back; and she fell to the ground dead.
sentences.i: Then she drew a sword she had by her, set its hilt in the ground and its point against her breast, and bore down on it until it came out through her back; and she fell to the earth dead.
sentences.n: qāʾim al-sayf, “the hilt”, literally “the upright (part)”. ṭaraf, “point, tip”. ṭalaʿa min, “to come out of”, colloquial. The shadda on خرّت is the print's.

sentences.t: فَحَزِنْتُ عَلَيْهَا وَنَدِمْتُ حَيْثُ لَايَنْفَعُنِي النَّدَمُ وَبَكَيْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥazintu ʿalayhā wa-nadimtu ḥaythu lā yanfaʿunī al-nadamu wa-bakaytu
sentences.l: And I grieved for her, and repented where the repentance does not profit me, and I wept.
sentences.i: I grieved for her, and repented when repentance could do me no good; and I wept.
sentences.n: The print runs lā yanfaʿunī together as one word, لاينفعني. ḥaythu, “where”, here “at a point when”, a common later use.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُمْتُ مُسْرِعًا إِلَى الْخِبَاءِ وَأَخَذْتُ مَاخَفَّ حِمْلُهُ وَغَلَا ثَمَنُهُ وَسِرْتُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِي
sentences.tr: thumma qumtu musriʿan ilā al-khibāʾi wa-akhadhtu mā khaffa ḥimluhu wa-ghalā thamanuhu wa-sirtu ilā ḥāli sabīlī
sentences.l: Then I rose hastening to the tent, and took what was-light its load and was-dear its price, and went to the state of my way.
sentences.i: Then I hurried to the tent, took whatever was light to carry and costly in price, and went on my way.
sentences.n: The print runs mā khaffa, “what was light”, together as ماخف. mā khaffa ḥimluhu wa-ghalā thamanuhu, “what was light of load and dear of price”, a stock rhymed phrase for portable valuables. sāra ilā ḥāli sabīlihi, “to go one's way, go about one's business”, a colloquial idiom.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ خَوْفِي وَعَجَلَتِى لَمْ أَلْتَفِتْ إِلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِي وَلَا دَفَنْتُ الصَّبِيَّةَ وَلَا الشَّابَّ
sentences.tr: wa-min khawfī wa-ʿajalatī lam altafit ilā aḥadin min aṣḥābī wa-lā dafantu al-ṣabiyyata wa-lā al-shābba
sentences.l: And from my fear and my haste I did not turn to anyone of my companions, nor did I bury the girl nor the youth.
sentences.i: In my fear and haste I gave no thought to any of my companions, and buried neither the girl nor the young man.
sentences.n: ʿajalatī: the print writes the final yāʾ undotted (ى), as it often does. iltafata ilā, “to turn towards”, here “to pay heed to”. ṣabiyya, “girl, young woman”.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ الْحِكَايَةُ أَعْجَبُ مِنْ حِكَايَتِي الْأُولَى مَعَ الْبِنْتِ الْخَدَّامَةِ الَّتِي خَطَفْتُهَا مِنْ بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi al-ḥikāyatu aʿjabu min ḥikāyatī al-ūlā maʿa al-binti al-khaddāmati allatī khaṭaftuhā min Bayti al-Maqdisi
sentences.l: And this tale is more-wondrous than my first tale, with the servant girl whom I snatched from the House of the Holy-place.
sentences.i: And this story is stranger than my first, about the servant girl whom I carried off from Jerusalem.
sentences.n: al-khaddāma, “the serving-girl”: so he calls the girl he kidnapped and sold. The kasra on بيتِ is the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ مِنَ الْبَدَوِيِّ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَبَدَّلَ النُّورُ فِي عَيْنِهَا بِالظَّلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni mina al-badawiyyi hādhā al-kalāma tabaddala al-nūru fī ʿaynihā bi-al-ẓalāmi
sentences.l: And when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard from the Bedouin this speech, the light in her eye was-exchanged for the darkness.
sentences.i: When Nuzhat al-Zamān heard these words from the Bedouin, the light in her eyes turned to darkness.
sentences.n: tabaddala … bi-, “to be exchanged for”: the light gave way to darkness. kalām and ẓalām rhyme, a touch of rhymed prose to close the scene.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
